newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Oct 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Oct 17.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
Government sources have confirmed that anyone found to be defying new laws banning handguns will face a prison sentence of 10 years.
LONRHO BREAK-UP HIT AS ANGLO SHUNS STAKE

The South African mining giant Anglo American's unwillingness to increase its 7.5 percent stake in Lonrho has scuppered the trading conglomerate's demerger plans. The group is understood to have reached its decision following a warning from the Ghanaian government that it would not be allowed to take control of Ashanti Goldfields, Lonrho's prime mining asset.
AMERICAN TRADE HOPES GIVE YEN STRENGTH
Ahead of tomorrow's U.S. trade figures for August, the yen staged a comeback overnight. It rose to 111.96 against the dollar from 112.285. Analysts expect any yen strength to be temporary.
THE STING THAT FLUSHED OUT THE SCAM ARTISTS

FBI agents posed for a year as brokers for a company called Thorton Capital, based on the 79th floor of the World Trade Centre in New York, in order to frame fraudsters. The ruse led to the round-up of 46 alleged penny stock promoters.
